title: automate-cross-account-route53-forwarding-and-secgrp-peering
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: private control plane installs in cross-account environments require automated DNS forwarding, secure ENI-based interface endpoints, and least-privilege security group peering rules. This PR adds Terraform modules and installer orchestration hooks to provision cross-account Route53 forwarding, create interface VPC endpoints with ENI attachments for the control plane, and a small Helm chart tweak to surface the controlPlane.vpcEndpointId setting. Summary: 1) New Terraform module terraform/modules/vpc-crossaccount-dns-forwarding that creates a Route53 outbound/inbound resolver association, IAM role for cross-account zone delegation, and conditional resource creation for hosted zones or delegated subzones. 2) VPC peering and security group automation in terraform/modules/vpc-peering-secgrp including explicit ephemeral rule creation, deny-by-default security group templates, and automated route table propagation for peering connections. 3) Installer orchestration changes in installer/upgrade to run a preflight DNS/peering validator and to annotate created endpoints for safe rollback. 4) Helm change to redwood-private/control-plane values to accept vpcEndpointId and configure internal service discovery via DNS suffix forwarding. Migration notes and rollbacks are included as outputs to the installer run. Backwards compatibility: module uses feature flags so existing single-account installs are unaffected. Testing: unit plan tests for Terraform modules, integration test that deploys two VPCs in the CI AWS account with delegated hosted zone, and manual validation steps in CONTRIBUTING docs.
commits: Add vpc-peering-secgrp module with ephemeral rules
Hook modules into installer provisioning flow
Add preflight DNS/peering validator and rollback annotation
Fix IAM assumptions for delegated zone association
Add tests for cross-account plan (mock) and docs
review_comments: Omar Velasquez: Please confirm that the cross-account IAM role only grants the minimal actions for hosted zone association. Also add a short note about TTL impacts on delegation.
Maya Chen: IAM role limited to route53:AssociateHostedZone and route53:DisassociateHostedZone and sts:AssumeRole. Added TTL note to installer/README.md.
Priya Nair: The peering route propagation could overlap with existing route tables in customer networks. Can we add an opt-out flag and safer default route table selection?
Maya Chen: Added opt_out_for_route_propagation variable and default selection logic to choose route tables tagged with redwood:control-plane=true. Documented behavior in module README.
Anton Karpov: CI plans failed on creds rotation. Suggest caching tfstate and mocking cross-account calls for unit tests.
Maya Chen: Split integration test to use mock provider for plan tests and a separate integration job that runs full provisioning with test accounts. CI updated.
Priya Nair: Approve after tests green.
Omar Velasquez: LGTM, approving the PR.

release_notes: Added Terraform module to automate cross-account Route53 forwarding and delegation
Automated VPC peering and least-privilege security group configuration for private control plane installs
Installer now performs preflight DNS and peering validation and annotates resources to support safe rollback
Helm control-plane values now accept vpcEndpointId to integrate with ENI-based interface endpoints
testing_instructions: Run ./scripts/ci/terraform-plan-crossaccount.sh which executes plan with mocked AssumeRole calls
For manual validation, follow tests/integration/crossaccount-dns/README.md to provision two test VPCs and validate DNS resolution across accounts
Use installer CLI with --dry-run to observe annotated resources before applying
Rollback: installer supports annotate-only mode and will remove created peering and route entries when run with --rollback flag and matching annotations
